collectors

##### Test Plan

We probably need to exclude archived charts from updating the ACLK during metadata replay  in 
```
#ifdef ENABLE_ACLK
    if (netdata_cloud_setting) {
        aclk_add_collector(host->hostname, plugin, module);
        aclk_update_chart(host, st->id, ACLK_CMD_CHART);
    }
#endif
```
The collector will be recorded as active by counting the number of charts it has created which is not the case (the actual /api/v1/info) will not return the collector in the list as it will be filtered by `rrdset_is_available_for_viewers`

The `aclk_update_chart` will be a no-op because
- The agent is set to `INITIALIZING` 
- The `aclk_update_chart` has an additional check to only allow updates from localhost
   - Note that the `localhost` has not been initialized during metadata log replay so the `host != localhost` check will always be true

The `aclk_add_collector` should be called when a chart changes from archived to non-archived (collection has started)

The `aclk_del_collector` should be called when a chart changes to archived

issue_context.title: Plugins.D language parsing in the metadata log and log replay
issue_context.body:
Open the metadata logs and integrate the incremental plugins.D parser to replay the log as defined [here](https://github.com/netdata/docs/blob/master/architecture/agent/db/database-log-format-pros-cons.md).

- load the metadata log file into memory.
- for each record in the log call the parser with the command.
- create the corresponding objects (rrdhost/rrdset/rrddim) and initialize them as inactive.
   - sane defaults for any collector state (e.g. last_collected)
   - export all the charts regardless of their state

Refactor rrdhost/rrdset/rrddim as needed to allow for partial initialization. There are going to be 2 states for all these objects:
1. inactive - the object has history but is not being collected
2. active - a collector has explicitly reinitialized the object

review_comments: This is a strange change as the list seems to have the defines, just in a different order. Keeping definitions in a sorted order prevents this kind of noise in the commit.
This doesn't look right. Why do you need the record bytes in the file to be aligned to steps of `RRDEND_BLOCK_SIZE`?
This is not actively being used at the moment. If we ever utilize the `METALOG_STORE_PADDING` command it's going to align the record.
Change to `debug` or remove.
Will do, but I need them in info for a little while to help with debugging. Same deal as the ACLK prints that remained `info()`. I will change this to `debug` as soon as I'm done testing compaction.
Why are we testing for this?
This may be an I/O error, permission error etc. Why shouldn't we test for this?
Ah, misread the code. This is indeed something else. If libuv has an internal error, such as out of memory, we do `fatal()`, otherwise we grab the I/O error, permission error etc and handle it.
The `ret<0` case is worth testing for (and handled in the next block), but the `ret!=req.result` seems a bit extreme (given the `POST` macro in the uv code).
Change to `debug` or remove.
Change to `debug` or remove.
There are other places where `rrdset_find_bytype_localhost` is used. Shouldn't be updated there as well?
But of course!
It's possible my brain deleted MacOS for known reasons.

The original `rrdset_find_bytype` in `rrset.c` should be removed instead of left as dead code.

I there a reason to move this to a `static inline` definition in a header file instead of an `inline` definition in the `.c` file like the original?

`rrdset_find_bytype()` is not dead code, it's being called by `rrdset_find_bytype_localhost()`, which is called by `rrdset_find_active_bytype_localhost()`. You could argue that `rrdset_find_bytype_localhost()` is dead code though.

When writing `rrdset_find_active_bytype_localhost()` I just wanted to make as few changes as possible, so I didn't refactor anything around it.
What will this be used for, and how will it be used?

The new endpoint to get archived charts is `/api/v1/archivedcharts`. You can query `127.0.0.1:19999/api/v1/archivedcharts` and get the list of charts that are archived. This is different than `/api/v1/charts` in that it only shows charts that no collector has touched yet. Those charts simply did not exist in the previous versions of netdata.

You can actually get the data of those charts by using the `/api/v1/data?chart=name` endpoint.

Those 2 endpoints are the only way this increment can deliver value to the users.
I don't think that end users will use the API. If I restart netdata can I see charts via the dashboard if they are archvied? Will they be visible to the cloud?

The requirements stated that the only way to get the archived charts would be via a new API call. So they should not be visible in the dashboard. About ACLK I'm not sure what to do, it's related to @stelfrag 's comment. We should discuss this.
I don't remember this point in the requirements - where is it (can I have a link?)
